method: Read immutable Git objects and compare width, prototype, operand grouping/evaluation, include prerequisite, ownership-declaration and serialization boundaries. Follow only named support headers; retain excluded implementation dependencies as open review actions.
failure_classes: missing include prerequisite or reinclusion guard

findings.evidence: include/curses.h:6 tests CURSES_H without defining it; repeated inclusion repeats struct _win_st.
findings.next_action: Compile isolated double inclusion, repair guard, and calibrate guard-removal control.

findings.evidence: include/curses.h:132-137 inserts win without grouping; clearok(&window, TRUE) binds member access before address-of.
findings.next_action: Exercise pointer expressions and getyx control-flow contexts, then repair grouping and add controls.

findings.evidence: include/stdio.h:179-190 defines getc/putc/getchar/putchar macros without corresponding function declarations.
findings.next_action: Probe parenthesized calls and function pointers; inspect actual archive symbols before completing declaration and definition repair.

findings.evidence: include/vmf.h:61-63 misgroups VMMODIFY(&segment), VSEG(a & b), and VOFF(1024 + 1).
findings.next_action: Compare compound inputs with independent arithmetic and field updates; repair grouping with calibrated controls.

findings.evidence: include/Makefile:50,54,64 suppresses recipe failures and loops can succeed after an earlier install failure.
findings.next_action: Inject a named installer failure in an isolated destination and verify exit status and output inventory.

findings.evidence: grp.h, lastlog.h, kmem.h and psout.h require undeclared prerequisite types/constants; structure headers have missing guards.
findings.next_action: Establish each installed interface contract, compare consumers and run standalone/double-inclusion probes.

limitations: Source inspection only; execution, actual callers and unlisted symlink targets were excluded.
Per-path residuals require implementation or interface evidence before behavioral closure.
A header declaration does not establish implementation correctness, hardware behavior or supported whole-standard conformance.
